# Router

AGENTS.md owns the request loop, the modes and the roster by kind. This
start finds where a request stands: an open or stopped change to resume, a
start to choose, or a new change to propose. The ledger guide owns the
change record's format.

Consumes: the request, the open or stopped change records under .greenline/ledger/ and the open or parked discussions under .greenline/ledger/discussions/

Next: the step the resumed change's "next" line names, the start the situation calls for, or frame under the mode the owner approves

## Resume a change

Read the open and stopped change records in the ledger, the
exact references in the request and the relevant files; the workspace's status
lists each change with its state and its "next" line. A change stopped on
another branch, local or remote-tracking, is found by its record's commit,
which every stop makes, and read from that branch. Read the candidates before deciding which change the
owner means: recency alone is not ownership. A record's "next" line names
the step reached and the action that resumes it. Resume there on the
change's branch, the one its record's commit sits on, switching to it
first when the session sits on another, and making a local branch from a
remote-tracking one; go on under the record's mode, with
no new proposal, and set the record's state `open` as your first write in
it. Ask only when several changes remain plausible, and say what each would
produce.

## What to work on

Asked what to work on, or what is up, list the stopped changes, each with its
"next" line, and the open and parked discussions, each with its idea and, for
a parked one, when it said to come back to it, from the workspace's status and
the records in the ledger. Recommend one with why, and wait for the owner's
pick: a change picked resumes as above; a discussion picked opens again on the
owner's word and runs as frame's references page says. Nothing is resumed,
opened or set before the owner picks.

## Choose the start

When this session holds a change and the request asks for another
change, stop that change first, as the ledger guide says. A
session that resumes, or is asked "what were we doing?", with no open or
stopped change on any branch says there is nothing to resume, proposes
nothing and asks the owner for the request. When no open or stopped change
is the request's, load the one start whose row in AGENTS.md names the
situation the request begins in, and no other; a start the owner names
runs. The orientation is a habit of the first change's frame, never a start
put before that change: `groundwork` runs inside it on an empty tree, and
`architecture-survey` loads only when the request asks for a survey or the
owner names it. A start that did not run is
never named in the record. A request that asks for a change and fits no
start goes straight to its proposal: the mode, then the line from `frame`.
A step asked for by name runs alone. ROUTING.md, the map of the line,
separates two methods that could produce different work.

## Watch the habits

While any step runs, watch for the situations the habits' rows in
AGENTS.md name. Load a habit only when the situation its row in AGENTS.md
names arises in the work at hand, never ahead of it or beside another habit
in case it might. `secrets` loads only where a secret is in reach: a key, a
token, a credential or a `.env` file that the work reads, writes, stages in
a commit or builds into an image, or a credential that may have leaked; a commit or
an image with none in reach loads nothing. `ponytail` loads only in its own
rows: before writing code the request leaves open, a refactor or a
simplification of code that works, a new internal API replacing an old one
that still has callers, or a question about what was deferred; writing code
the request plainly asks for is none of them. A habit whose output is a
durable file the owner did not ask for is offered in one line and made on
the owner's yes.

# The map of the line

Read this when two methods could produce different work. It describes the
corpus's methods, not a promise that all are installed: the roster in
AGENTS.md lists what is installed, and an absent skill is unavailable even
when named here. The request's authority carries through the line; ask
about an unresolved product decision or a scope boundary, never for
permission to read a skill.

## The steps

A change's mode runs the steps in this order, each at the depth the mode
table in AGENTS.md gives it, and you never choose among them. Each step's
skill writes its section of the change record
when the step ends.

| Step | Its section of the record holds |
| --- | --- |
| `frame` | the intent restated, what is out of scope, the settled terms and the open questions |
| `plan` | acceptance that can fail and the work in ordered tasks; when the work splits, the plan directory's spec and its tickets file, a mode beside each ticket |
| `anticipate` | the claims the build rests on, attacked before the build; it is careful's premise review |
| `build` | what was built, the deviations from the plan and the approaches dropped; the commits carry the change's trailer and the checks are recorded |
| `review` | each reviewer's findings and what was done with each |
| `verify` | each acceptance item verified, not verified or inconclusive, with its evidence |
| `close` | the decisions and terms the change settled, the state, the "next" line and the cost |

A step asked for by name runs alone: "grill me" is `frame`, a spec or
tickets is `plan`, a stress test of a plan is `anticipate`,
"review this branch" is `review`, "verify this" is
`verify`, and a decision or a term to write down is `close`. It needs no
mode and no record while it changes no file. Once it edits a file, a
write into the knowledge homes (the decisions book, the ADR home and the
glossary) included, it opens a change and its proposal like any other
edit, and `close` opens a quick record first.

## Resuming

An open or stopped change resumes at the step its "next" line names, on
the branch its record's commit sits on, under the record's mode, and the session that resumes it sets
it `open`. Its earlier sections record what was done, and the builder's
sections are the builder's claims, not evidence. A ticket of a plan
directory opens its own change record under the mode beside it in the
tickets file, on the planning change's branch, and the record omits the
steps its plan's record holds.

## Two methods that look alike

| The situation | Choose | Not |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Observed behavior is wrong and its cause is unknown | `diagnose`, a start: a reproducer and the cause, then the repair as a change | `verify`, which proves a claimed outcome |
| A design question inside one change | `frame`, at its depth | `wayfinder`, a start that maps a decision space spanning sessions |
| Which product idea to build next | `what-to-build`, a start that proposes in the reply | `frame`, which shapes a request already chosen |
| The structure of the code as a whole | `architecture-survey`, a start that surveys and reports | `review`, which judges one change's commits |
| A brittle or slow test suite | `sweep-tests`, a start with its mutation proof | `review`'s excess lens, which reads one change |
| The repository lacks its baseline | `groundwork`, a start that sets up only what the purpose needs | `build`, which works inside a baseline |
| An idea the owner brings is still vague | `idea-refine` (trial), a start that varies it, stress-tests it and states its assumptions before any change | `what-to-build`, which proposes ideas from the repository's own evidence |
| The repository's quality bar is unwritten, or a check was loosened to reach green | `constraint-driven-development` (trial), a start that writes the bar down and guards it | `groundwork`, which sets up the baseline a bar measures |
| A promise an order of events or an input no test reached could break | `verify-formally`, a start that checks a model or a bound and keeps the check in step with the code | `verify`, which proves a change's claims on the code as it runs |
| How a part of the code works, or the map of its subsystems | `explain`, a start that traces it from the code and keeps the atlas's pages | `architecture-survey`, which surveys the whole structure for deepenings |
| A mechanism to explain as a figure | `anatomy`, a habit that builds an interactive figure of a real object driven by a truth model | `show-me`, which draws the reply's text views |

Use evidence available locally before asking the owner a factual question.
When two plausible tasks remain, explain the difference in the intended
result. Routine implementation choices stay with the agent inside the
settled scope.

its glossary, or `GLOSSARY.md` when it has none.

## Where its work lands

The ledger is `.greenline/ledger/`, its guide `.greenline/ledger/README.md`, which owns the change record's format and the stop; each change's record is `.greenline/ledger/<id>.md` and its folder `.greenline/ledger/<id>/`. `greenline status` lists each change with its state and its "next" line. A change's checks run through `greenline check`. Working files live under `.greenline/tmp/<id>/`, and `greenline tidy` removes them when the change is done, never a cited file. Each discussion's record is `.greenline/ledger/discussions/<id>.md`, which `greenline status` lists with its state and its idea; the ledger guide's "Discussions" gives its form and its states.

## Floor debt

Where `.greenline/ledger/interface/paths.json` gives a route floor findings, or `greenline status` reports interface drift, list them as floor debt among the next things to work on, each with its route and its rule.

## Marks

Where the status line prints `marks:`, list the owner's open marks among the next things to work on, each with its id, its address and its note, from `greenline mark list`: the ones on an open change's address are that change's follow-up, and the rest are the next proposal's input.
